rationale: C20 is an earlier Mother's Day proclamation using substantially the same operative machinery and highly similar language: it cites the same 1914 joint resolution, directs government officials to display the flag on government buildings, and calls upon the public to honor mothers by displaying the flag at homes or other suitable places. The child expands the commemorative recitals and forms of public and private expression, but C20 plausibly supplied a concrete, material drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas by a joint resolution approved May 8, 1914 (38 Stat. 770), the Congress designated the second Sunday in May of each year as Mother's Day
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Congress, by a joint resolution approved May 8, 1914 (38 Stat. 770), set aside the second Sunday in May as Mother's Day
shared_material.explanation: Both invoke the same resolution in nearly identical language as the legal basis for the annual proclamation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I direct the appropriate officials of the Government to display the flag of the United States on all Government buildings on that day.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I ... direct the appropriate officials of the Government to arrange for the display of the flag of the United States on all public buildings on Mother's Day
shared_material.explanation: The principal governmental directive is nearly verbatim, with only minor wording changes.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I also call upon the people of the United States to give public and private expression of their love and reverence for the mothers of America ... by display of the flag at their homes or other suitable places.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I call upon the people to display the flag on that day at their homes or other suitable places as a public expression of honor for our mothers.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts the predecessor's public appeal, preserving the flag display at homes or other suitable places as an expression honoring mothers.
